2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}) as your last tool call and then stop. ## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md
- /figma-generate-design — for translating an app page or layout into Figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-generate-design/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## claude.ai tldraw
Use `search` to query the tldraw Editor API spec (e.g. search for methods by category or name). Use `exec` to run JavaScript on the canvas — your code receives `editor` (the tldraw Editor instance) and helpers like toRichText, createShapeId, createArrowBetweenShapes. The current canvas state is kept in model context as raw TLShape, asset, and binding data.

## plugin:small-business:shopify
This server helps users set up and manage their Shopify stores.

## Store Creation
Users who don't have a store yet can use get-new-store-previews to create one from a short description.
After calling get-new-store-previews, encourage the user to browse the previews and pick the theme they like best.
Each preview has a signup link — signing up through it creates a real Shopify store with that theme and matching products pre-installed.
Encourage continued brainstorming: users can try different descriptions, tweak ideas, or explore new directions without commitment.

## Store Management
Once a store exists, this server provides tools for managing it:
- Products: search, create, update, bulk-update status, and organize into collections.
- Collections: search, create, update, and manage product groupings.
- Orders: list recent orders and get detailed order information.
- Customers: list and search customers.
- Inventory: check inventory levels and set quantities at specific locations.
- Analytics: run ShopifyQL queries for sales, order, and product performance data.
- Discounts: create percentage-based discount codes.

## GraphQL — General-Purpose Access
The Shopify Admin API exposes hundreds of resources. The built-in tools above are optimized shortcuts for common operations (with structured output and widgets), but they only cover a subset of the API.
When the user asks about a resource that has no dedicated built-in tool — such as gift cards, metafields, metaobjects, pages, blogs, markets, translations, publications, and many others — fulfill the request with the GraphQL Workflow below. NEVER tell the user that data is unavailable just because there is no built-in tool for it.

1. If a built-in tool matches the request, prefer it (better UX).
2. If no built-in tool matches, run the GraphQL Workflow below. Do NOT open with graphql_query or graphql_mutation — the workflow starts at graphql_schema.

I've found comprehensive information about the tax implications of renting free-standing photovoltaic (PV) systems on agricultural land in Germany. Here are the key findings:

## Classification and Asset Categorization

When agricultural land is leased for free-standing PV systems, it falls out of agricultural and forestry assets into basic assets due to the non-agricultural use.

## Tax Consequences

**Grundsteuer (Property Tax):**
Instead of property tax class A for arable or grassland, property tax class B applies to free-standing PV systems, with an exception only in Bavaria, where property tax class A continues to apply to free-standing systems.

**Erbschaftsteuer (Inheritance Tax):**
Because the property falls out of agricultural assets, the agricultural special rules for inheritance no longer apply, resulting in a higher valued area being inherited. Under current law, agricultural land leased for PV free-standing systems no longer qualifies as agricultural and forestry assets, leading to the loss of inheritance and gift tax benefits.

The valuation is based on market value, which increases due to high lease income, accordingly raising the inheritance tax assessment base.

## Potential Solutions

The BDEW demands legislative clarification assigning PV free-standing systems to agricultural assets during limited use, suggesting either a separate PV benefit provision with flat-rate valuation deductions or a simple regulation in the valuation law treating PV systems as temporary, public-interest special use with partial inheritance tax relief.

## Solarpaket I und benachteiligte Gebiete - Länder-Opt-out

Das Erneuerbaren-Energien-Gesetz (EEG 2023) ermächtigt die Länder per Verordnung Solar-Freiflächenanlagen auch in benachteiligten landwirtschaftlichen Gebieten bei dem Zuschlagsverfahren für Solaranlagen des ersten Segmentes zu berücksichtigen (§ 37c EEG 2023).

Die Bundesländer können im Wege entsprechender Rechtsverordnungen bestimmen, dass Gebote für Projekte auf Flächen, deren Flurstücke zum Zeitpunkt des Beschlusses über die Aufstellung oder Änderung des Bebauungsplans als Ackerland oder als Grünland genutzt worden sind, die in einem benachteiligten Gebiet lagen, im Zuschlagsverfahren nicht zu berücksichtigen sind, vor dem 1. Januar 2031, wenn und solange auf mehr als 1 Prozent der landwirtschaftlich genutzten Flächen des jeweiligen Landes Freiflächenanlagen betrieben werden.

Seit dem Inkrafttreten des Solarpaketes I am 16. Mai 2024 wurde die Vergütungsfähigkeit für Anlagen auf Acker- oder Grünland in benachteiligten Gebieten auf nicht ausschreibungspflichtige PV-Anlagen erweitert.

Solche Verordnungen haben in der Vergangenheit Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Hessen, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Saarland, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt und Thüringen erlassen.

## Key Information About JStG 2024 and Free-Field Photovoltaic Systems

According to § 158 Paragraph 1 of the German Valuation Act (BewG), property that is no longer used for agricultural and forestry purposes is classified as general real estate property for tax purposes.

### Current Situation and the 2025 Regulation

This classification results in the loss of tax benefits for agriculturally used land, particularly regarding property tax. When farmers provide land for free-field photovoltaic installations, the land no longer counts as agricultural and forestry property but as general real estate, resulting in higher property tax.

### Proposed Solutions

ECOVIS has developed a draft law proposal that was forwarded to the federal government by associations and electricity producers, which would treat land used for free-field photovoltaic installations as agricultural and forestry property for tax purposes.

### Regional Exception

Bavaria has announced that starting in 2025, property tax on free-field photovoltaic installations will be reduced, as these areas will be included in the more favorable Property Tax Class A.

## Current Legal Situation

Currently, agricultural land loses its tax privileges under inheritance and gift tax when leased for photovoltaic purposes. A leased area for operating free-space photovoltaic systems is excluded from agricultural property under inheritance tax and is classified as non-privileged real estate, with valuation based on land value.

## Tax Burden Impact

In practice, since there are typically no land value benchmarks for solar free-space systems, the financial administration assumes 50% of the value for the nearest commercial area. This can result in significant valuation increases for agricultural land when converted to solar use.

## Proposed Legislative Changes

The BDEW (German Association of Energy and Water Industries) has made proposals for legal changes, suggesting that agricultural land should not completely lose its tax benefits when leased for free-space systems. A core proposal is that agricultural land used for free-space photovoltaic systems should continue to be assigned to the agricultural business for inheritance and gift tax purposes.

## Limited Success to Date

A positive response has so far only come from Bavaria, where the ground tax for free-space systems is being reduced from 2025, as the areas are included in the more favorable ground tax category A.

The search results indicate that while legislative changes are being proposed and discussed, there has not yet been a comprehensive federal law change implemented on this issue as of mid-2026.

Based on the search results, here's comprehensive information about GAPDZV § 12 and Agri-PV eligibility:

## Key Regulations and Eligibility

According to § 12 Abs. 5 GAPDZV, an Agri-PV system is defined as a solar energy installation on agricultural land that does not exclude land cultivation using standard agricultural methods, machines and equipment, and reduces the agriculturally usable area according to DIN SPEC 91434:2021-05 by no more than 15 percent.

## Funding Eligibility (85 Percent)

When these conditions are met, 85 percent of the agricultural land remains eligible for funding. The condition is that agricultural use is not significantly restricted in its intensity, duration, or type of cultivation.

## DIN SPEC 91434 Standards

The DIN SPEC 91434 defines standards and framework conditions so that Agri-PV systems can be uniformly planned and evaluated.

## Categories I and II

Category I consists of elevated systems with a minimum clearance height of 2.10 meters and a maximum 10 percent land loss. Category II includes ground-level and vertical systems with a maximum 15 percent land loss.

## Recent Changes (2026)

The previous cap of 85 percent for Agri-PV land has been abolished in recent updates. According to more recent information, eligible funding now depends on the actual degree of impairment rather than a fixed 85 percent ceiling.

## Artikel 32c der Raumplanungsverordnung (Agri-PV)

Seit dem 1. Juli 2022 regelt die Raumplanungsverordnung die Standortgebundenheit von Agri-PV Anlagen ausserhalb der Bauzone spezifischer.

### Voraussetzungen für Agri-PV-Anlagen

Gemäss Art. 32c Abs. 1 Bst. c RPV können Solaranlagen mit Anschluss ans Stromnetz ausserhalb der Bauzonen insbesondere dann als standortgebunden gelten, wenn sie in wenig empfindlichen Gebieten Vorteile für die landwirtschaftliche Produktion bewirken oder entsprechenden Versuchs- und Forschungszwecken dienen.

Darüber hinaus muss die Agri-PV-Anlage auf Fruchtfolgeflächen zu einem höheren Naturalertrag im Pflanzenbau führen.

### Gebietliche Anforderungen

Der Begriff «wenig empfindlich» wird näher definiert als «anschliessend an Bauzonen oder bestehende Infrastrukturen» und generell «möglichst geringe entgegenstehende Schutzanliegen».

### Rechtliche Besonderheiten 2025

Am 15. Oktober 2025 hat der Bundesrat eine Änderung der Raumplanungsverordnung beschlossen. Der erste Teil gilt seit dem 1. Januar 2026, der zweite Teil ab dem 1. Juli 2026.

Diese neuen Regelungen zielen darauf ab, den Bau grosser PV-Anlagen in der Landwirtschaftszone zu ermöglichen, wobei die landwirtschaftliche Produktion aufrechterhalten bleiben soll.

content.content:
# Agri-PV Rechtslage Schweiz – Zusammenfassung

**Raumplanungsgesetz (RPG Art. 32c) – Änderungen 2026:**
Seit 1. Januar 2026 sind Solaranlagen auf landwirtschaftlichen Nutzflächen bewilligungsfähig, wenn sie „die landwirtschaftlichen Interessen nicht beeinträchtigen und Vorteile für die landwirtschaftliche Produktion bewirken" oder Forschungszwecken dienen. Entgegenstehende Schutzinteressen (Natur-, Gewässerschutz) können Bewilligung verhindern.

**Fruchtfolgeflächen:**
Bei wertvollen Kulturlandkategorien müssen landwirtschaftliches Ertragspotenzial und maschinelle Bewirtschaftungseignung erhalten bleiben.

**Bewilligung:**
Baugesuch erfolgt bei der Gemeinde; kantonale Fachstellen prüfen Raumplanungsrecht. Frühe Abstimmung mit kantonalen Behörden empfohlen.

**Direktzahlungen:**
Flächen mit Agri-PV-Anlagen (nicht von nationalem Interesse) erhalten Direktzahlungen, wenn sie nachweislich bewirtschaftet werden als Ackerfläche, Dauerkultur oder ganzjährig geschützter Anbau.

**Einmalvergütung:**
Nicht erwähnt im Dokument.

# Agri-PV 2026: Faktische Kennzahlen

**EEG-Zuschlagswerte Agri-PV (Gebotstermin 01.07.2026):**
- Höchstwert: 5,90 ct/kWh
- Durchschn. mengengewichteter Zuschlagswert: 4,79 ct/kWh
- Aufschlag hoch aufgeständert (≥2,10 m): +0,5 ct/kWh
- Anzulegender Wert bis 1 MW (Inbetriebnahme 01.08.–31.12.2026): 6,59 ct/kWh

**GAP-Direktzahlungen (85%-Grenze):**
Keine Abschaffung dokumentiert. Gültige Regelung: „max. 15 % Flächenverlust" bei GAP-Beihilfefähigkeit (§ 12 GAP-Direktzahlungen-Verordnung, Ländererlasse 15.07.2022). Die 85%-Nutzbarkeit ist DIN-SPEC-Anforderung, nicht GAP-Regel.

**Investitionskosten:**
900–1.700 €/kWp für Anlagen 0,5–2 MWp (Fraunhofer ISE, 2024)

**Pachtwerte (Logic Energy Portfolio 2024):**
1.000–3.500 €/ha/Jahr (Doppelnutzung)

**Kategorie-I-Mindesthöhe:**
2,10 Meter lichte Höhe (DIN SPEC 91434:2021-05)

**§ 35 BauGB Agri-PV:**
Hofnahe Anlagen bis 2,5 ha Grundfläche, eine Anlage je Hofstelle, privilegiert im Außenbereich (keine Bebauungsplanpflicht)

The criteria apply to ground-mounted solar installations (PV-Freiflächenanlagen) under the regulations introduced by Solarpaket I.

## Five Minimum Criteria

The document outlines **five naturschutzfachliche Mindestkriterien**:

1. **Claimed Land Area** (Beanspruchte Grundfläche) – Requirements regarding land use considerations

3. **Passage for Animal Species** (Durchgängigkeit für Tierarten) – Ensuring wildlife corridor connectivity

4. **Biotope Elements** (Biotopelemente) – Integration of habitat features within installations

5. **Soil-Conserving Operation** (Bodenschonender Betrieb) – Minimizing soil disturbance during operations

## Compliance Requirements
While the document structure indicates these are minimum standards that must be met, the specific thresholds, timelines, and exemptions are detailed in the full guidance document itself.

According to § 37 Abs. 1a and § 48 Abs. 6 EEG 2023, operators of funded PV ground-mounted systems must fulfill at least three of five nature conservation minimum criteria. The choice of which three criteria to fulfill is left entirely to the operator of the PV system.

The five minimum criteria include three facility-related criteria (numbers 1, 3, 4) and two operational criteria (numbers 2 and 5).

Regarding the 60 percent ground area limit you mentioned: These measures concern the maximum ground area used, soil care and soil protection, wildlife corridors and biotope elements.

To limit additional burden on facility operators, they can select three criteria from a list of five that best fit local conditions. It is legally possible to switch between the minimum criteria during the facility's operating period, as long as at least three are always fulfilled.

content.content:
# PV auf Acker/Grünland in benachteiligten Gebieten seit Solarpaket I

**Rechtslage: Opt-out statt Opt-in**

Seit 16. Mai 2024 wurde das System umgestellt. Früher mussten Länder aktiv per Verordnung zustimmen (opt-in). Jetzt sind "alle als Acker- oder Grünland genutzten benachteiligten Gebiete" grundsätzlich freigegeben. Länder können sich davon abweichen (opt-out).

**Bedingungen:**
- Anlagen bis 1 MW: keine Ausschreibung nötig (ab 15. Mai 2024)
- Anlagen über 1 MW: Ausschreibungspflichtig (ab 31. Dez. 2016)
- Gebotsmenge: max. 50 MW pro Gebot (derzeit aber 20 MW bis EU-Genehmigung)
- Bebauungsplan erforderlich (ab 1. Sept. 2003)
- Mindestens 3 von 5 Naturschutzkriterien erforderlich

**Länder mit Ausschlussregelungen:**

Die Quelle nennt Länder, die historisch Verordnungen erlassen haben (Baden-Württemberg, Bayern, Hessen, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Rheinland-Pfalz, Saarland, Sachsen, Sachsen-Anhalt, Thüringen), erwähnt aber nicht explizit, welche aktuell Opt-out nutzen.

input.message:
## Report: ÖkoInvest pages for land owners and farmers

All 7 routes are built. Each one returned 200 at 1440 and 390 px with no runtime errors, and I viewed the screenshots. For the wizard, the decision tool and both calculators I also scripted the clicks through to the result state and checked it (tooltips as well). ESLint on my files is clean. The Node self-test gives the expected numbers: 10 ha in southern Germany ≈ 9.1 MWp ≈ 10.0 GWh/a, and a fixed lease of 10 ha × 2,800 € = 28,000 €/a. Nothing is committed.

**Most important finding:** with the current values in `markt.js`, the Agri-PV figures don't add up. For 10 ha vertical Agri-PV, investing yourself gives about 0 % IRR and a payback of about 30 years. The cooperative share comes out at about −1.5 %. At the same time the calculator assumes an investor pays 1,600 €/ha rent, which that project economics could not support. The causes are `AGRI.opexProKwp` = 14 (solar parks now use 9), the Agri-PV investment costs, and the tariff (4.8 ct for vertical, 5.3 ct only for high-mounted systems). I did not change those existing values. Please have someone review `AGRI.capexProKwp`/`opexProKwp` and `PACHT.agriProHa` together. The calculator now notes that on-farm self-consumption, storage and saved hail nets are not included.

### Routes and files
- **`/freiflaeche`**: what we develop, criteria for the land, the EEG eligible-land rules, approval in DE/AT/CH, ecology, dismantling and guarantees, FAQ. It has an SVG cross-section of a solar park with numbered labels and a legend, and a 2–4-year timeline shown as a bar chart.
- **`/agri-pv`**: DIN SPEC 91434 categories I and II, four systems each with its own SVG drawing, a system comparison table, crops and livestock, benefits (land-use efficiency 160 %, and 186 % in the 2018 heat summer, from Fraunhofer's Heggelbach pilot), rules for GAP, building law and EEG, economics, FAQ.
- **`/flaeche-verpachten`**: the four lease models calculated for 10 ha, a bar comparison against arable farming, what is in the contract (8 clauses), cautiously worded tax notes, "what we check", 6 steps to the first payment, a portal box, the `flaeche` form, FAQ.
- **`/landwirte`**: the four routes as cards and a table, why Agri-PV suits farms, the interactive "Welcher Weg passt?" tool (5 questions, recommendation with reasons, all routes scored), the `agri` form, FAQ.
- **`/flaechencheck`**: a 4-step wizard with the `ov-step-vor/-zurueck` animation. The result shows the traffic light, a score gauge, every scoring point with its reason, MWp, GWh, lease per year and over 30 years, the Agri-PV and carport options, and next steps. The `flaeche` form sits right below and sends all inputs plus the result as `daten`. The scoring logic is explained on the page.
- **`/rechner/pacht`**: fixed, indexed or revenue share (with a minimum lease), term, lead time with reservation premium, and a comparison with arable rent and gross margin. It has an SVG chart of cumulative income with a tooltip.
- **`/rechner/agri-pv`**: renting vs. investing yourself vs. cooperative share, side by side. It shows investment, first-year energy income, IRR (via `irr`), payback, remaining GAP payment and the farming gross margin. Selecting "Obst & Beeren" switches the system to high-mounted.
- Files: the pages above, plus
  - components in `src/components/Flaeche/` (`SolarparkSchnitt`, `Zeitleiste`, `FlaechenWizard`, `PachtRechner`, `MobilKurz`)
  - components in `src/components/Agri/` (`AgriBild`, `wege`, `WegeEntscheider`, `AgriPvRechner`)
  - logic in `src/lib/rechner/{pacht,agriPv,flaechencheck}.js`
- Test script: `scratchpad/selbsttest.mjs`. Screenshot helpers in `scratchpad/pw/`: `teile.mjs` (sections), `montage.mjs` (mobile in columns), `a_*.mjs` (click actions).

### Changes to `markt.js` (additions only)
- `AGRI.kulturen`: 4 crops, each with a gross margin and a farming-yield factor per system (source noted as a comment).
- `AGRI.beteiligungAnteil`: range 5–49 %, default 20 %.
- While I was working, someone else updated `ERLOESE`: no separate Agri-PV sub-segment yet, only a +0.5 ct bonus for high-mounted systems. I aligned all page texts and the logic: vertical systems get 4.8 ct, high-mounted get 5.3 ct. The merchant phase now uses `merchantSteigerung`.

### Fact check on the briefing
- **JStG 2024 claim not confirmed:** I could not find that JStG 2024 keeps leased PV land in agricultural assets. As of June 2026 BDEW is still calling for a fix to inheritance tax (pv magazine). So the texts say: under current practice such land usually loses the agricultural status, Bavaria differs on property tax, the rules are in flux, see a tax adviser. Please correct the briefing.
- **Confirmed and written up cautiously:**
  - Since Solarpaket I (May 2024), land in disadvantaged areas is eligible unless a state opts out (possible once solar parks cover more than 1 % of its farmland).
  - Subsidised solar parks must meet 3 of 5 nature-protection criteria.
  - The GAP rule (85 % of Agri-PV land stays eligible) still applies.
  - In Switzerland the planning rules for Agri-PV changed in 2026.
  - For Austria I describe the Grünland-PV zoning and the environmental-impact check (UVP) only in general terms.

### Other open points
- These pages link to planned routes that don't exist yet: `/genossenschaft`, `/solarcarport`, `/prozess`, `/registrieren?rolle=flaeche`.
- The dev server on port 3100 restarted by itself several times while I was working (connection refused), probably because of parallel builds by other agents.

### Requests for shared files
- `AnfrageFormular`: a longer button label wraps onto two lines on desktop. Suggest `whitespace-nowrap` on the button. I worked around it with shorter labels.
- `MobilKurz` (the sticky mobile results bar) is in `src/components/Flaeche/`. It could move into `Rechner/bausteine.js` so all calculators share it.
- Navigation, `tools.js` and the sitemap: the routes `/freiflaeche`, `/agri-pv`, `/flaeche-verpachten`, `/landwirte`, `/flaechencheck`, `/rechner/pacht` and `/rechner/agri-pv` need to be added or checked there. The tool IDs `pacht`, `agri-pv` and `flaechencheck` already exist in `TOOLS`.
